# Reading the tide tables

The harbour office publishes a tide table every December for the next year.
Each row lists the time and height of one high water or low water.

## Heights

Heights are measured in metres above chart datum, the lowest tide that
the survey expects to see. A negative height means the water falls below
datum, which only happens during spring tides.

## Spring and neap tides

Spring tides follow the new moon and the full moon. The range between high
and low water is largest then. Neap tides follow the quarter moons and the
range is smallest.

## Planning a crossing

The sandbar at Grey Point dries at 1.8 metres. A keel boat drawing two
metres must cross the bar within one hour of high water.
